title: feat(processors): YOLO detection for v8, v11, and v26
body:
## Summary

Adds a `yolo` processor for YOLOv8, YOLO11, and YOLO26 detection, and keeps `yolo_v8` as a permanent alias. MediaMolder still ships no weights. The node is behind the `with_onnx` build tag.

- The pure-Go decoders read either a raw head (`[1, 4+nc, N]`, per-class NMS) or an end-to-end head (`[1, max_det, 6]`, NMS already applied). Layout comes from the tensor shape.
- `yolo` letterboxes with pad 114 and bilinear resize, takes class names from the model when `labels_file` is omitted, and returns empty metadata when inference ran and found nothing. `class_id` is always present (`0` is a real class). `face_detect` and `vidi_analyzer` write `-1`.
- `yolo_v8` keeps black nearest-neighbour letterbox, class-agnostic NMS, `"unknown"` labels without a labels file, and nil metadata on an empty frame. A dynamic-shape export still loads on the alias and fails on `yolo`. When the file has a concrete shape, both nodes allocate from that shape.
- The exported ONNX type is `YOLODetector` in `processors/yolo_onnx.go`. The guide moved to `docs/yolo-guide.md`; `docs/yolov8-guide.md` is a one-line pointer.
- Examples 69 and 70 are YOLO11 and YOLO26 graphs. They skip when the model file is absent. Examples 29–32 stay on the alias.

`.gitignore` also ignores `.bash_history`.

## Test plan

- [x] `go test ./...`
- [x] `go test -tags with_onnx ./...`
- [x] Docs reviewed against `processors/yolo.go`, `processors/yolo_onnx.go`, and the metadata writers

title: perf(av): speed up moving_crop_scale resampling
body:
## Summary

`moving_crop_scale` resampled each frame on one thread, rebuilding the kernel for every source row and every output pixel, and filled the frame black before overwriting the covered pixels. This keeps that kernel and makes the common path faster.

- Separable weights are built once per frame. They stay unnormalized, and each pixel divides by the norm once, in the same tap order, so the pixels match.
- Planar 8-bit and sole little-endian wide samples load and store directly. Packed and big-endian frames stay on the generic path.
- The weight tables and the horizontal buffer live on the processor and are reused across frames. `Close` frees them, including when sample matching reports an unused keyframe.
- Rows of a frame at least 256×128 run on threads created and joined inside the cgo call.
- `FillBlack` runs only when some output pixel is left unwritten. A window that covers every luma centre overwrites every pixel.

`neighbor` and `area` stay on their existing loops. swscale is not used, and `SwsReinits` stays 0.

A local 1920×1080 to 1280×720 set, across several formats and kernels, matched the previous pixels byte for byte and dropped from 24.2s to 2.8s.

## Test plan

- [x] `go test ./av/ -run 'TestFillBlack|TestResampleWindow'`, including a 320×180 threaded bilinear pass and a second pass through the same scratch buffer
- [x] `go test ./processors/ -run TestMovingCropScale`
- [x] `go test ./job/ -run 'TestMovingCropScale|TestHandleGoProcessor_RecordsSwsReinits|TestHandleGoProcessor_TimeBaseDrivesMovingCropScale'`
- [x] The same av and processor tests with `-race`
- [ ] CI

title: feat(processors): add moving_crop_scale
body:
## Summary

Adds `moving_crop_scale`, a go processor that crops each video frame to a keyframed window and scales that window to a fixed output size. The encoder opens at that size through `FrameTransformInfo`, so the graph does not need a following `scale`.

This replaces a separate path-crop processor. A trim is `match: sample` with `unmatched: drop`: each keyframe is used at most once, a frame must land on that keyframe or strictly inside half the gap to the next one, and `Close` fails if a keyframe matched no frame. The old `path_crop` name and its `width` / `frames` job shape are not accepted.

Other behaviour:

- `match: bracket` (the default) does not consume keyframes. An exact PTS uses that keyframe. Between two keyframes every frame is interpolated, including the midpoint. Before the first and after the last, `unmatched` applies (`hold` by default, or `drop` / `error`). A frame with no PTS is dropped under `hold` and `drop`, and is a `Process` error under `error`.
- Interpolation is `hold`, `linear`, or Catmull-Rom `smooth`. Sample matching requires `hold`. A `zoom` list interpolates `log(w)` and `log(h)`. `zoom` is output-relative: `w = output.width / zoom`.
- Zoom is inclusive from 1/16 to 64. Init rejects a keyframe outside that range, and a side below 1 pixel. After interpolation, a positive size is clamped into `[output/64, output×16]`. A side that collapses to 0 or below is an error.
- The window may sit partly or fully outside the source. Missing pixels are digital black, so a 16:9 picture can become a 9:16 frame with bars. `aspect: output` derives the height from the output aspect. A derived height taller than the picture hangs off the frame.
- Position is sub-pixel. Each output pixel is sampled at `x + (i+0.5)·w/outW − 0.5`, so an integer 1:1 window still copies source pixel `x+i`. Kernels are `neighbor`, `bilinear`, `bicubic`, `lanczos`, `area`, and `spline`. On a downscale, bilinear, bicubic, Lanczos, and spline widen with the window. Spline always resamples. The other kernels copy with `CropRect` only when the window is integer, inside the picture, chroma-aligned, and the same size as the output. Taps outside the source contribute black and stay in the weight sum.
- `align` is still accepted so an older job opens. It does not snap to the chroma grid. `emit_rect` posts the window rounded half away from zero, and the origin may be negative. The frame's sample aspect ratio passes through. `SwsReinits` stays 0 because the node resamples the window itself (`av.Frame.FillBlack`, `av.ResampleWindow`).
- `t` keyframes convert on the first video frame with `av.SecondsToTicks`. `ProcessorContext.TimeBase` is the input edge time base. Hardware frames, interlaced frames, and floating-point, paletted, bitstream, and bayer frames are errors.

The branch also carries the runtime and frame-crop work that the closed path-crop PR (#78) needed: forwarding a processor frame that has no metadata, releasing delay-buffer frames, and `CropColumns` / `CropRect` / `CropWindow`. There is no `path_crop` node in the tree.

The Inspector edits output size, the interpolation and match options, and one row per keyframe. Choosing sample matching sets interpolation to hold. The Align dropdown is gone. The Run panel shows `[sws ×N]` when the rebuild count is non-zero.

## Tests

- `av`: `CropRect`, `CropWindow`, `VisibleHeight`, `Scaler`, `SecondsToTicks`, `FillBlack`, and `ResampleWindow` (integer copy, quarter-pixel shift, hang-off black, area, Lanczos, 10-bit high bits, spline blur, downscale kernel stretch, chroma following the luma edge, pixel-centre extent, rgb565, packed 10-bit).
- `processors`: `TestMovingCropScale` covers init rejection, zoom bounds, √2 zoom, aspect centring, the letterbox, Catmull-Rom, half-away rounding with `align` ignored, the odd visible width scaled rather than trimmed, the fast-path left edge, a sub-pixel blend, hardware and interlaced rejection, `t` keyframes, and sample matching (half-step, one use, one tick, far PTS, unused `Close`).
- `job`: stream-info transform on the encoder edge, time-base driving `t` keyframes, `SwsReinits == 0`, a bracket end-to-end job with no trailing `scale`, and a sample-match end-to-end job (`copy_ts`, input `ss`/`to`, left edges, and `Close` failing on a keyframe past the source).
- `frontend`: `tsc -b --noEmit`. `TestCuratedNodesResolveToRealEntries`.

## Notes

- `align: "8"` is not implemented. The keyframe UI is a row editor, not a timeline.
- The embedded GUI binary is unchanged until `make build-gui-static`. The Inspector change is in the frontend sources.
- `.bash_history` and `docs/architecture/proposals/blur-detection.md` are left untracked.

title: fix(smartcopy): constant-rate DTS, AAC trim head, hvc1 HEVC cuts
body:
## Summary

Three smartcopy output defects reported against #77, all reproducible with `ffmpeg`/`ffprobe` and `mediamolder run` on 80-frame 29.97 fps fixtures (GOP 12, two B-frames) cut mid-GOP at both ends:

1. **Cuts from constant-rate B-frame sources had uneven DTS steps** (a 6006-tick jump at the head, a 1 + 2001 pair at a join), which completed-file probes reject as variable frame rate.
2. **Re-encoded AAC lost the head of the window**: the output started one AAC frame late behind a 21 ms empty edit.
3. **An `hvc1` HEVC source gave an `hev1` cut**, which AVFoundation does not decode at all.

## Changes

- **DTS.** `sendRun` extrapolates the run's first DTS values one frame at a time from the run's first frame instead of reading the priming GOP, and `emitCopy` retimes a copied keyframe whose leading pictures were re-encoded with the run (its source DTS sits those frames too early). The frame tick and the source reorder depth come from the GOP's own PTS steps rather than the demuxer's average frame rate. The cut tests now assert every DTS step is one frame for H.264 closed/open GOP and HEVC, including the open-GOP cut-position sweep.
- **AAC.** The auto-inserted `atrim` is followed by `asetpts=PTS-STARTPTS` (unless `copy_ts`), and the sink treats channels fed through an `__atrim__` node as internally trimmed: no ss/to drop or stop, no start shift, only segment re-anchors (minus the rebase). The encoder's priming packet (−1024 samples) and the packet holding the window's first samples now reach the muxer. Both sink loops take the cut compare and the anchor from shared helpers; `-shortest` compares written (post-shift) PTS on every channel.
- **hvc1.** HEVC config mode: a trial x265's VPS/SPS/PPS are renumbered to ids the source does not use (Exp-Golomb fields rewritten, trailing bits re-padded) and appended to the output hvcC; every re-encoded slice header is renumbered to the new PPS id with its slice data kept byte-aligned. The track keeps the source's sample entry. An hvcC source whose sets cannot be renumbered fails the job rather than falling back to `hev1`; in-band remains only for Annex B sources.
- Docs (`smartcopy.md`, `json-config-reference.md`) and CHANGELOG updated.

## Verification

- `repro.sh` from the report: all three fixtures give `41×1001` DTS steps with no clamps; the AAC cut is `start_time 0`, duration 1.401000, first packets −1024/0, and its decoded samples are identical to the `ffmpeg -af atrim,asetpts -c:a aac` reference (max |diff| 0 over the file); the HEVC cut is `hvc1` and `AVAssetReader` decodes 42/42 frames (the H.264 cut, avcC with two SPS/PPS, decodes 42/42 as well).
- New tests: constant-DTS assertion in the cut tests; `TestAudioTrimAACKeepsHeadOfWindow` (sine source, unaligned start); `TestHEVCRenumberRoundTrip` on real x265 output (ids read back, slice re-parses, slice data byte-identical) plus `TestLastOneBit`, `TestHvcCWithParamSets`, `TestBitBufUE`; `TestSinkWriter_TrimmedChannelShift` and `TestSinkWriter_TrimmedChannelCutAndShortest` for rotation re-anchoring and `-shortest` on a rebased channel.
- `go test ./job ./av ./processors ./internal/gui ./cbs/...` pass; `go vet` and `gofmt` clean.

title: feat(processors): add path_crop
body:
## Summary

Adds the `path_crop` go_processor: crop each video frame to a full-height window whose left edge follows a per-PTS path of centre-x samples, dropping frames that are not on the path. It is the reframing step of a 16:9 → 9:16 pipeline whose analysis stage writes the window centre per frame.

Three commits:

1. **fix(job): forward go_processor frames returned without metadata.** The runtime only swapped in a processor's output frame inside the metadata branch, so a processor returning a new frame and nil metadata had its output ignored: the original frame went downstream and the new one leaked on every frame. Also fixes a nil-pointer `Close` when a processor drops a frame while returning metadata. Regression tests included.
2. **feat(av): `Frame.CropColumns` built on `av_frame_apply_cropping`.** FFmpeg's own window math (same as the `crop` filter) with `AV_FRAME_CROP_UNALIGNED`, copied into aligned buffers, so 8-bit, high-bit-depth, semi-planar and packed formats are all cut correctly. Plus `Frame.Log2ChromaW` and `PixFmtByName`.
3. **feat(processors): add `path_crop`.** Params `width` and `frames: [{pts, cx}]`. Frames match the nearest unused sample within half the smallest path step; left edge is `cx − width/2` rounded (ties lower), clamped, aligned to the chroma step. `Close` fails the job when a sample matched no frame (missing `copy_ts`, a time-base-changing filter, or a source that ends early). Docs in `docs/path-crop-processor.md`, GUI palette entry, README and CHANGELOG.

## Tests

- `processors/path_crop_test.go`: registration, left-edge rule vectors, lossless left-edge test on painted frames, PTS matching and ties, `Close` reporting, every `Init` failure.
- `av/frame_crop_test.go`: plane offsets on yuv420p, yuv420p10le, nv12, rgb24; side-data copy; range checks.
- `job/go_processor_replace_test.go`: runtime forwards replacement frames without metadata; drop without metadata.
- `job/path_crop_e2e_test.go`: `copy_ts` job with input `ss`/`to`, `format`, `path_crop`, window `scale`, `setpts`, `sidedata` over a lavfi source encoded with ffv1 writes one frame per path sample at the expected left edges (skips without a system `ffmpeg`).

## Notes

- The encoder opens at the size of the last filter before the processor (a `go_processor` with inputs cannot report its output size), so jobs follow `path_crop` with a `scale` to `width` × frame height.

title: fix(smartcopy): make boundary GOPs decodable and keep open-GOP frames
body:
## Summary

Two smartcopy bugs, both reproducible with `ffmpeg` and `mediamolder run` alone:

1. **Re-encoded boundary GOPs did not decode** (H.264 and HEVC, MP4 and MOV). Boundary packets were forwarded as Annex B, referring to the encoder's own SPS/PPS, while the track kept the source's avcC/hvcC. Decoders read the start codes as NAL lengths and parsed the slices against the wrong parameter sets, so every re-encoded frame was dropped or garbled.
2. **Open-GOP sources lost in-window frames.** GOPs were grouped in decode order, so a GOP's leading pictures (displayed before its keyframe) were dropped at both cuts.

## Changes

- Re-encoded packets are re-framed to the source's NAL framing (length-prefixed for avcC/hvcC sources).
- **H.264 + libx264:** the boundary encoder takes a free `sps-id`; its SPS/PPS are appended to the output avcC. Track stays `avc1`, copied packets byte-identical.
- **HEVC, and H.264 with other encoders:** parameter sets travel in-band, the source's VPS/SPS/PPS are re-inserted on copied keyframes, and MP4/MOV outputs get `hev1` / `avc3`. Applied on both sink stream-registration paths.
- GOPs are classified by presentation span; consecutive boundary GOPs form one re-encoded run; the leading pictures of the copied GOP after a head cut join that run.
- Splices: CRA→BLA for HEVC; for H.264 the copied slices' `pic_order_cnt_lsb` and `frame_num` are shifted in place until the next IDR (fixed-width fields, slice data untouched). Without this libavcodec reorders or drops frames at the head cut on open-GOP x264 sources.
- Re-encoded packets carry durations and display-order DTS (the MP4 edit list otherwise cut the run's last frame; DTS collisions at joins made movenc reject packets). The boundary encoder's B-frame depth and reference count are kept within the source's.
- `smartcopy_global_header` is ignored; the GUI toggle is removed (embedded bundle rebuilt).
- Docs: `docs/smartcopy.md` "How it works" and limitations; CHANGELOG entry.

## Tests

- `job/handlers_smartcopy_cut_test.go`: generated 64×64 fixtures (80 frames, GOP 12, two B-frames) for H.264/HEVC, open/closed GOP, MP4/MOV. Cuts are decoded with the stream's own extradata and checked for frame count, order, content and `decode_error_flags`; plus a cut-position sweep over open-GOP sources and an in-band H.264 run with `h264_videotoolbox` (skips where unavailable).
- `job/smartcopy_nal_test.go`: NAL framing, avcC/hvcC, CRA→BLA, RBSP escaping, prefix-overflow refusal.
- `go test ./...`, `go vet`, frontend `tsc`/lint, `make build-gui-static` pass.

## Known residuals

- Open-GOP H.264: a head cut within a few frames of a non-IDR keyframe can make libavcodec log `mmco: unref short failure` (copied slices' MMCO ops address pictures before the cut); the decode is correct.
- AVFoundation playback of `hev1` / multi-SPS avcC is not verified.

title: raw: DecodeDevelopScaled shrinks the master from LibRaw's output, across the CPUs
body:
A consumer that only ever shows a bounded master (a viewer's 4096-pixel grid) had to take the full-sensor `NRGBA64` from `DecodeDevelop` — 185 MB for a 24-megapixel sensor — and shrink it with its own per-pixel scaler. Measured on an M1 Pro with a D750 NEF: 1.45 s of develop + transcode, then 1.39 s of `x/image/draw` CatmullRom, for a 4096×2738 result.

## `DecodeDevelopScaled(path, maxPixel)`

Resamples LibRaw's packed RGB16 buffer straight into the bounded `NRGBA64` (`scale.go`, pure Go, every build):

- A separable Catmull-Rom (a = −0.5) with `x/image/draw`'s shrinking semantics: the support widened by the scale so every source sample is weighed, the kernel argument scaled by 1/scale, taps clipped to the source and the weights renormalised at the edges. Against `x/image`'s result on the real NEF: max difference **1/65535** per sample, ~100 % equal.
- Both passes across the CPUs by rows, in **chunks of 64 destination rows**: each chunk shrinks only the window of source rows it reads (neighbouring windows overlap by the kernel's support, shrunk again), so nothing sensor-sized is built but LibRaw's own buffer. The result does not depend on the number of workers.
- The same 24-megapixel develop is **1.3 s all in** (the scale 60 ms); 105 MB allocated per call instead of ~290.
- Nothing is enlarged: a bound the sensor is within returns the full size. `DecodeDevelop` is the same call with no bound; its full-size transcode now runs across the CPUs too. The stub build declares both.

## Tests

- Size rounding (a consumer's: `int(w·f + 0.5)`, never enlarge, a row never rounds to nothing); every source sample weighed by some tap with weights that sum to one and indices inside the source; a flat field stays flat at every pixel, alpha opaque; a ramp stays a ramp (monotone, each interior pixel the ramp's value at its own centre); the pixels are identical with 1, 7 and more-workers-than-rows; an overshooting lobe is clamped, not wrapped; the transcode is big-endian and opaque.
- With LibRaw: the scaled fixture develop equals the full develop shrunk through the same function; a bound within the sensor returns the full master; colour space and version are the develop's.
- `BenchmarkScale24MP`: ~60 ms.

Reviewed (two passes, every finding folded). No new dependencies, no cgo changes, no OS-specific code.

title: av: select the encoder's sample format through avcodec_get_supported_config (FFmpeg 9 removed AVCodec.sample_fmts)
body:
## What

FFmpeg 9 removed `AVCodec.sample_fmts` (deprecated since 7.1). `select_supported_sample_fmt` in `av/encode.go` still read it, so the `av` package no longer compiled against a current libavcodec (63.1) — on MSYS2 the `ffmpeg` package moved to 9.0.2 on 2026-10-01 and every cgo build of a host application broke:

```
av/encode.go:35:15: error: 'AVCodec' has no member named 'sample_fmts'
```

The function now reads the encoder's supported sample formats through `avcodec_get_supported_config`, exactly as `codec.go` already does for pixel formats, sample formats and sample rates. Behavior is unchanged: an encoder that lists no formats accepts any; a chosen format that is not listed falls back to the first listed one. The `-Wdeprecated-declarations` pragma goes with the field.

## Verified

- Built (`go build ./...`, `go vet ./av`) and the `av` tests run against **libavcodec 63.1.102 (FFmpeg 9.0.2)** — MSYS2 ucrt64 — and against **62.28.100 (FFmpeg 8.1)** — MSYS2 mingw64.
- Nothing else in the module reads a field FFmpeg 9 removed: the only other `sample_fmts` / `pix_fmts` uses are filter-graph strings and a `get_format` callback parameter.

Note for anyone building on Windows: FFmpeg 9's `avfilter` links `ggml` (the whisper filter), so a runtime that stages libav DLLs now needs `ggml-0.dll` and friends beside them.

title: fix(job): source node skips undecodable packets like ffmpeg; name AAC/AC-3 parser errors; surface go_processor Close() errors
body:
## The bug

A 40-minute camcorder MPEG-TS (h264 + AC-3) with **two** damaged audio frames produced no output at all: the graph source node returned the first decoder error as fatal and the run died with

```
averror(-16976906): Error number -16976906 occurred
```

`ffmpeg -i tape.ts -vn -f null -` over the same file logs `Error submitting packet to decoder` twice and finishes at 40:24 — skipping a rejected packet is FFmpeg's default (`-xerror` opts into abort). `-16976906 = -0x1030C0A` is libavcodec's **private** `AAC_AC3_PARSE_ERROR_SYNC` (`aac_ac3_parser.h`), which `ac3dec` returns raw and `av_strerror` cannot name.

## What changed

- **`job/handlers_source.go` + new `job/decode_errors.go`** — a per-stream `decodeErrorGate`: a packet the decoder rejects (`SendPacket`, `ReceiveFrame`, the end-of-stream drain, subtitle decode) is counted in the node's `Errors` metric (which existed and was never incremented) and skipped; 1000 consecutive failures still fail the run; one summary log line per damaged stream. `EAGAIN` from `SendPacket` stays fatal (a loop bug, not damage). A demuxer-flagged corrupt packet is logged and still handed to the decoder, as ffmpeg does without `+discardcorrupt`. No `avcodec_flush_buffers` — libavcodec has consumed the packet, and a flush would drop good reference pictures.
- **`global_options.exit_on_error`** (config + both schemas) — ffmpeg's `-xerror`.
- **`av/err.go`** — the `AAC_AC3_PARSE_ERROR_*` family is named (`AC-3/AAC parser: frame sync error (AAC_AC3_PARSE_ERROR_SYNC)`), with `av.ErrCodeAACAC3Parse*` and `av.IsCodecParseError`.
- **`job/handlers.go` / `engine.go`** — `graphRunner.close()` returns the joined go_processor / event-sink `Close()` errors and `runGraph` reports them when nothing earlier failed. A processor that does its real work at close time (speech-to-text over its whole buffer, a file-writing hook) had no other way to report failure, and its partial result was being thrown away.

## Tests

- `job/decode_errors_test.go` — the policy, pure Go.
- `job/source_decode_errors_test.go` — an AC-3-in-mpegts fixture the engine builds itself, with holes punched in the elementary stream (null-packet substitution: the tape-dropout shape; garbling payload bytes does not work, AC-3 conceals bad mantissas silently). The damaged file reproduces the wild signature exactly (`corrupt input packet` → `AAC_AC3_PARSE_ERROR_SYNC`), decodes end to end with 6 errors skipped and 95% of samples kept, fails under `exit_on_error`, and survives truncation / scribble / bit-flips.
- `job/graph_runner_close_test.go` — a close-time processor error reaches `Run`; the run error wins over it.
- `av/err_test.go` — naming + classification.

`go test ./av/ ./job/` green except `TestNodePerfTracker_*` (`Elapsed = 0s`), which fails identically on a clean `main` here — Windows timer granularity, unrelated.

title: feat(bitstream_trace): CSV, derived POC, rate analysis, captions, validation
body:
## Summary

Second round on the bitstream tracer (#70): CSV output, typed coded-picture
records with a derived Picture Order Count, per-unit class / per-packet time
for bit-rate analysis, 608/708 caption carriage dumps, and a first-class
validation layer (`violations[]`, opt-in structure checks, `--validate`).
13 commits, review-driven — two review rounds are folded in.

Report schema bumps to `mediamolder.bitstream_trace/2` (shape change: slices
report a `picture` object instead of a summary map). Text output stays
byte-for-byte FFmpeg `trace_headers` parity — all golden tiers unchanged.

## What's new

**CSV format** (`output_format: csv`, `--format csv`) — one row per NAL unit /
OBU, leading with the group-by columns `kind, class, name, packet`, then packet
context, unit identity, dedicated picture columns (1:1 with the JSON record),
and a compact-JSON `summary` column for non-picture units. Rows are assembled
by column name, so header reorders can't misalign values.

**Typed picture records** — H.264/H.265 slices report a fixed-schema
`picture` object (`type`, `poc`, `frame_num`/`segment_address`, `lsb`, `pps`,
`qp_delta`, `ref_l0/l1`, `idr_pic_id`, `field`, `first_slice`, `dependent`)
instead of a free-form summary. Substantially smaller on slice-dominated
streams; other unit types keep their content summaries.

**Derived POC** — Rec. H.264 §8.2.1 (all three `pic_order_cnt_type` modes,
lsb/frame_num wrap, mmco5 post-reset semantics, fields) and Rec. H.265 §8.3.1
(prevTid0 tracking with RADL/RASL/SLNR exclusion, IDR/BLA resets, continuity
across mid-stream CRAs; dependent slice segments reuse the picture POC and
inherit the independent segment's fields). Validated against x264 (even
2×display-order POCs, per-IDR resets) and x265 (continuous numbering across
CRA-opened GOPs) output, plus hand-computed spec edge cases.

**Rate analysis** — every unit gets a `class` (`vcl` / `ps` / `sei` / `other`;
AV1 frame-header/tile-list OBUs count as `vcl`), every packet `time` and
`dts_time` in seconds. Bit rate over time split into picture payload vs SEI
overhead is a one-line aggregation; the guide has the pandas recipe.

**Captions** — T.35 SEI and AV1 ITU-T T.35 metadata summaries carry
`raw_hex` (bounded) and, when the ATSC A/53 / SCTE-128 wrapper matches
(0xB5 / 0x0031 / GA94 / cc_data), `cc_count`, `cc[]` triplets and
`contains: [cea608|cea708]`. A dump, not a decoder. Unregistered user data
gets the same `raw_hex`; `--units caption` selects the carrier units.

**Validation** — always-on `violations[]` (layer 0): every unit parse failure
and fragment split failure, located by packet/unit with the parse diagnostic.
Opt-in structure checks (layer 1, `--checks default|strict|<ids>`):
`vcl_before_ps`, `frame_num_gap` (errors, `default`), `no_aud`,
`sei_after_vcl` (warnings, `strict`) — riding the existing decode-order walk,
so range/unit filters never hide findings. `--validate` exits non-zero on

title: feat: bitstream trace — H.264/H.265/AV1 NAL/OBU analysis to JSON
body:
Packet-level bitstream analysis for H.264, H.265 and AV1 — an improved,
machine-readable version of FFmpeg's `trace_headers` bitstream filter.
A new `bitstream_trace` graph node and `mediamolder trace-headers` CLI
report every NAL unit / OBU in a stream — parameter sets, slice/frame
headers, SEI messages, and optionally every syntax element with bit
positions — to a JSON, JSON Lines, or text file, with **no decoding**.

Built on a new cgo-free **`cbs/` package**: a read-only, line-for-line Go
port of libavcodec's Coded Bitstream framework (`cbs.c`, `cbs_h264*`,
`cbs_h265*`, `cbs_av1*`, `cbs_sei*`, `h2645_parse.c`), following the
project rule of porting FFmpeg's C as the reference implementation.

Design doc: `private_local/bitstream-trace-proposal.md`
(branch `proposal/bitstream-trace`). User guide: `docs/bitstream-trace.md`.

## What's in the box

- **`cbs/`** — bit reader, exp-Golomb/leb128/uvlc primitives, FFmpeg's
  trace-callback model, Annex B + avcC/hvcC/av1C splitting with
  emulation-prevention removal, the SEI framework, and the full read-side
  syntax templates for all three codecs with parameter-set/reference
  state. Struct, field and element names mirror the C sources so the port
  can be audited line-for-line.
- **`cbs/report/`** — `json` (streamed document) / `jsonl` / `text`
  writers; detail levels (`summary` | `headers` | `elements`); unit-type
  filters with cross-codec family aliases (`sei` matches HEVC
  `SEI_PREFIX`/`SEI_SUFFIX`, …); inclusive `packet_range` / `max_packets`
  through one shared gate; per-unit summaries (SPS dimensions + VUI, PPS
  coding tools, slice types, SEI inventory with decoded HDR/user-data
  payloads, AV1 sequence/frame headers and metadata).
- **`bitstream_trace` go_processor** — a self-opening `FrameSource`
  (nothing in the graph decodes); references its input via top-level
  `input_id`; optional per-packet events for GUI progress. GUI catalog
  entries included; example job `testdata/examples/68_bitstream_trace.json`.
- **`trace-headers` CLI** — same driver; `--format text` reproduces
  `ffmpeg -bsf:v trace_headers` output byte-for-byte for direct diffing.
- **`av`**: new `StreamExtraData` and `Packet.Pos` accessors.

## Improvements over FFmpeg's trace_headers

- Structured output with packet/unit indices, byte offsets and sizes,
  EPB positions, and derived summaries — not interleaved stderr text.
- A malformed unit is recorded on the unit and parsing continues;
  `trace_headers` aborts on the first error.
- Units FFmpeg silently drops (HEVC layered NALs, reserved types) are
  listed with a `skip` reason.

## Correctness

- **Golden conformance**: checked-in captures of the reference FFmpeg
  build's `trace_headers` output over checked-in ≤10 KB fixtures
  (x264/x265/SVT-AV1; `scripts/gen-cbs-fixtures.sh` +
  `scripts/gen-cbs-golden.sh`). Two tiers: cgo-free (raw elementary
  streams as one fragment) and full-driver (avcC/hvcC/av1C MP4s + IVF,
  including the `Extradata` section and diagnostics). All three codecs
  match **byte-for-byte**.
- **Fuzzing**: `FuzzH264/H265/AV1ReadPacket` (~1M execs each, clean).
  Template unwinding uses panic/recover at the unit boundary; a runtime
  panic is converted to `InternalError` and asserted absent — hostile
  input can never crash the process.
- Unit tests for the bit reader, exp-Golomb/leb128 limits, EPB removal,
  NAL splitting, avcC parsing, range/filter contracts, error isolation;
  processor + engine integration tests; example 68 runs in
  `TestExamplesRun`. `go test ./...` green.

## Notes for reviewers

- Two changes outside the feature: **(1)** `job/engine.go` routes
  edge-less graphs (a single self-opening go_processor) through graph
  mode — the linear path assumed ≥1 output and panicked; **(2)** the
  three duplicated output-path sanitizers (fileWriteHook, whisper,
  split_manifest_writer) are folded into
  `processors.sanitizeProcessorOutputPath` — error text now names the
  right processor, behaviour otherwise unchanged (whisper's volume-aware
  variant won).
- `resolveClipInputIDs` and `frameSourceConsumedInputs` gain top-level
  `input_id` support (validation + runtime), used by the new node.
- No schema changes (`processor`/`params` are already open); no frontend
  type changes; the node uses the generic params editor in the GUI.
- Goldens are pinned to the reference FFmpeg tree (`e2f2c1ea`); when that
  tree updates, rerun `scripts/gen-cbs-golden.sh` and diff — a mismatch
  is an upstream CBS change to port.

## Deliberately deferred (tracked in the proposal)

`PacketConsumer` inline packet tap (in-graph tracing + smartcopy reuse),
`AV_PKT_DATA_NEW_EXTRADATA` side data, derived POC in slice summaries,
pts-window `packet_range`, H.264 MVC/SVC decomposition (absent upstream
too).

## Test plan

- `go test ./...` (includes golden, fuzz seed corpus, examples run)
- `go test ./cbs/ -fuzz FuzzH264ReadPacket -fuzztime 60s` (repeat per codec)
- `mediamolder trace-headers --format text file.mp4` vs
  `ffmpeg -i file.mp4 -c copy -bsf:v trace_headers -f null -` on any
  H.264/H.265/AV1 file

title: sequence_editor: video clip reader seeks to source_in
body:
## Problem

The video `clipReader` positioned by decoding from the start of the file and counting frames at the source's nominal fps — `getFrameAtSeconds` discarded the entire prefix on every fresh reader or jump. Measured on a 2 h, 26.8 GB DV-in-AVI capture (single-clip trim through the job engine):

- window at 5:32 → **~13 s** before the first frame
- window at 60:00 → **~2m24s**

The audio side of the same processor had the identical defect, fixed in #67. This PR mirrors that fix on video.

## Fix

On a fresh reader or a forward jump past `seekMinAheadSec` (~2 s):

- `SeekFile` to `seekSlackSec` (1 s) before the target, `FlushBuffers`;
- decode until the first frame with a usable timestamp re-anchors the absolute frame index — **bounded** by `maxLandingFrames`, and frames without a position are discarded, never emitted (an all-NOPTS source must not be decoded to EOF while landing — #67's one review must-fix, kept out of the video path);
- landed past the target (coarse index / long GOP): double the slack (1→2→4→8 s) and retry; exhausted → decode-from-start once, `noSeek` set, never retried;
- from the anchor, the existing nominal-fps counting covers the remainder; the small-advance continuation path (`lastSrcSec`) is untouched — transitions and cached readers keep the warm decoder. Backward jumps keep today's semantics (no rewind).

The seek/landing constants are shared with `sequence_audio.go`.

Anchoring uses a new `av.Frame.BestEffortTimestamp()` rather than `PTS()`: containers that store only decode timestamps (AVI tape captures) decode **every** frame with `pts == NOPTS`, so pts-anchoring would have sent the primary use case straight to the fallback. (The old comment blaming `SeekFile` for immediate failures dates to the initial timeline renderer, which trusted the landing blindly and PTS-matched individual frames.)

## Results (same 2 h capture, fresh reader per window)

| window | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 5:32 | ~13 s | 29 ms (31 frames decoded) |
| 60:00 | ~2m24s | 56 ms (31 frames decoded) |

Landing is within one frame of the request (`ts=3600.007` for the 60:00 window; DV is intra, so the slack second is the whole cost).

## Tests

`processors/sequence_editor_seek_test.go`, template #67's audio tests, with a test-visible `frames` decode counter:

- **SeeksToSourceIn** — mpeg2video-in-AVI (the dts-only shape tape captures present): fetch at 50 s of a 60 s long-GOP file decodes <200 frames, not the ~1250-frame prefix; the returned frame's timestamp proves position; continuation decodes ≤2 frames with no second seek.
- **NearHopDoesNotSeek** — a 1 s hop decodes-and-discards (≥20 frames, no landing); a 7 s hop seeks (≤100 frames). Both directions asserted.
- **LandingIsBounded** — the landing state machine never anchors on NOPTS frames and stops at `maxLandingFrames` (no demuxer here can produce a file whose post-seek frames stay NOPTS — the raw mpegvideo demuxer synthesizes timestamps — so the state machine is driven directly, as #67's audio bound test does).
- **UnanchorableSourceFallsBack** — a reader that cannot place frames degrades to exactly the old decode-from-start behaviour, frame count pinned.

`go test ./processors/ ./av/` green; `gofmt -s`/`go vet` clean (the seven pre-existing `gofmt -s` complaints on main are untouched).

title: av: frame field flags and DetectInterlace — which field first, from the cheapest source that knows
body:
av: frame field flags and DetectInterlace — which field first, from the cheapest source that knows

A deinterlacer (bwdif, yadif) has to be told the field parity, and many sources
do not say: a DV tape capture in an AVI carries an "unknown" codecpar field
order, and content re-encoded without field signalling has progressive-looking
flags over combed pictures.

- Frame.Interlaced / TopFieldFirst / SetFieldFlags expose
  AV_FRAME_FLAG_INTERLACED and TOP_FIELD_FIRST; Frame.MetadataValue reads a
  frame-metadata entry (idet writes its verdicts there).
- DetectInterlace(input, stream, maxFrames) answers in order: codecpar when it
  says anything; the decoder's per-frame flags over the first frames (DV,
  MPEG-2, interlaced H.264 set them from the bitstream); idet's combing
  analysis of those same frames for unflagged interlaced content; and the
  codec's own rule for DV (NTSC 480 lines bff, PAL 576 tff). The report says
  which source decided and carries the tallies.
- Decision thresholds: flags win when at least half the frames carry them;
  idet decides when it classified at least half the frames and one side
  leads, else unknown — a deinterlacer is never applied on a guess.

Tests: the classifier table, the flag round trip, the DV rule, and the
detector on lavfi frames — a moving mandelbrot is progressive; tinterlace-woven
frames are tff from their flags, and still tff from idet with the flags
stripped. testsrc2 is documented as unusable for the progressive case: its
alternating-line chart detail reads as combing to any field detector.

On a real NTSC DV-in-AVI capture: bff, decided by the decoder flags (48/48),
with idet agreeing (47 bff).

title: processors: sequence audio seeks to source_in and survives layout-less PCM
body:
Two defects in the sequence_editor's audioReader, one cause visible, one not:

1. PCM sources whose decoded frames carry no channel layout (WAV, DV/AVI tape
   captures) made libswresample refuse every frame as INPUT_CHANGED. ingest()
   dropped them silently, the FIFO never filled, and fill() demuxed the file to
   EOF looking for samples that never came — on an interleaved 27 GB AVI that is
   the whole file read at disk speed, and the clip's audio was silence either way.
   The frame's layout is now pinned to its channel count before the resampler
   sees it, and a reader whose frames keep failing gives up after 16 in a row
   instead of reading to EOF.

2. A clip placed deep into its source decoded from the start and discarded —
   source_in=T cost T seconds of audio decode (and T seconds of video demux on
   an interleaved container) before the first sample. getSamples now seeks to
   one second before the target, lets the first decoded frame's PTS re-anchor
   the absolute position, and discards exactly the remainder. Hops under 2 s
   stay on decode-and-discard; sources that hand back no PTS after a seek fall
   back to the old path once and are not retried.

Measured on a 2 h DV-in-AVI capture: an 8 s trim at 0:00 went from 68 s to
1.1 s with its audio restored (-25 dB, matching the source, was -91 dB).

Tests: a Go-written stereo WAV (layout-less PCM) pins non-silence, a
sample-exact landing at 50 s of a 60 s file in a few dozen packets, and that a
1 s hop does not seek.

Not in this PR: the video `clipReader` still decodes from the file start to `source_in` by design (`getFrameAtSeconds` counts frames; the comment records that `SeekFile` misbehaved on some sources). On the same capture a trim at 60:00 takes 2m24 for that reason alone now that audio is fixed. A keyframe-seek + decode-forward-by-PTS for the video reader is the follow-up.

title: feat(whisper): expose n_max_text_ctx — the long-form repetition lever
body:
﻿Exposes `n_max_text_ctx` (the whisper.cpp CLI's `-mc`) as `WhisperOptions.MaxTextCtx`, plus a `max_context` param on `whisper_stt`.

## Why

whisper decodes long audio as a chain of 30 s windows inside **one** `whisper_full` call, and by default prompts each window with the text decoded from the previous one. That is a positive-feedback path with ~224 tokens of memory: an emitted phrase raises its own prior for the next window, which re-emits it, which re-seeds the prompt. Above a threshold it runs to end-of-file.

This is the well-known Whisper long-form failure. Every production stack disables the feedback — OpenAI `condition_on_previous_text=False`, faster-whisper, whisperX, and whisper.cpp's own CLI via `-mc 0`.

Measured on a 48-minute stereo tape capture, **worst verbatim repeat**:

| audio | default | `MaxTextCtx = 0` |
|---|---|---|
| clean | 57 | **26** |
| our downmix | 1,250 | **27** |
| scaled by √2 | 1,238 | **15** |

Capping at 15–27 *regardless of the audio* is the fingerprint of removing a feedback path rather than nudging a threshold — what's left is just the per-window token budget. It also explains the chaotic sensitivity we measured: a **≤1 LSB** difference in otherwise identical audio flipped worst-repeat between 57 and 1,250, and only a feedback path amplifies a perturbation that far.

## Not a new default

The trade is real: cross-window context genuinely helps phrasing, and disabling it cost **~9% fewer unique lines** on clean audio. Short files don't have the problem at all. Batch whole-file callers want `0`; streaming callers — whose every call is already a short window — do not. Upstream's own position is that disabling it "should give worse results in general", which is the right posture for a general-purpose library.

## `*int`, not `int`

`0` is the interesting value, so it cannot double as "unset" the way `Threads <= 0` can. A plain `int` would have made Go's zero value silently disable prompt conditioning for **every existing caller** the day the field was added — an additive struct field that is secretly a breaking behaviour change.

## Two guards, because both fail silently

`Validate()` refuses combinations whisper.cpp accepts and then mishandles without complaint:

- **`MaxTextCtx = 0` with `InitialPrompt` set.** The initial prompt reaches the decoder *only* through the same prompt-history path `n_max_text_ctx` gates, so `0` discards it entirely. The caller gets a plausible transcript and no indication their prompt was ignored. `InitialPrompt` is already public API here, so this is reachable today.
- **`MaxTextCtx = 1`.** whisper.cpp 1.8.4 computes a take-count of `(n - 1 - 1)` and indexes backwards from `prompt_past.end()` by it; at `1` that's `-1`, reading out of bounds. Usable domain is `{0} ∪ [2, ∞)`.

## Also corrects a false claim this repo shipped

The `RematrixMaxval` comment from #65 (and its diagnostic test) asserted the √2 downmix gain was "the whole cause" of the loops. **It was not** — the loops survived that fix unchanged. `RematrixMaxval: 1.0` stays, rejustified on the correct grounds: parity with whisper.cpp's own reference loader, which downmixes by averaging and never leaves ±1.0.

## Tests

`applyMaxContext` is split out of `Init` so the mapping and its rejections are testable without loading a model — model load aborts outright when ggml has no compute backend beside the test binary. Covers: absent leaves the default, `0` is honoured rather than treated as unset, positives pass through, all three rejections, and that a rejected value is never left applied.

`av` suite green. In `processors`, `TestMetadataWriter_*` and `TestTwelveLabs*` fail identically on clean `main` — pre-existing, unrelated.

## Known, deliberately not in this PR

`whisper_full_default_params(BEAM_SEARCH)` sets `beam_search.beam_size` but leaves `greedy.best_of = -1`, and both strategies read `greedy.best_of` for the decoder count at every fallback rung — so asking for beam search currently gets 1 sample per fallback where greedy gets 5. Real defect, worth its own commit, and explicitly **not** a repetition fix (measured: `-bo 5` was mildly *worse* on this content than `-bo 1`).

title: fix(whisper_stt): normalize the stereo downmix; whisper was being fed +3 dB
body:
﻿A stereo tape capture (PCM s16, 32 kHz, 48 min) transcribed as **one phrase repeated 1,236 times** across 30 minutes. The same file decoded to 16 kHz mono by the ffmpeg CLI, handed to the **same model with the same parameters**, transcribed fine — so the defect lives in the conversion between, not in the decoder or the model.

## Measured, not guessed

Three suspects looked plausible in `accumulate`/`resampleAppend`. A diagnostic that runs the processor's own path over the file and dumps the buffered PCM eliminated all three:

| suspect | verdict |
|---|---|
| rebuild-on-any-`ConvertFrame`-error drops the delay line | **0 rebuilds** — one format across all 93,187 frames; never entered |
| output frame's `nb_samples` unset before `ConvertFrame` | misread — `swr_convert_frame` allocates, as `ConvertFrame`'s own contract says |
| nothing flushes at EOS | false — `Close` has always called `drainResampler` |

What the dump actually showed: sample count exact (2908.71 s vs the container's 2908.709899 s), and **peak 1.3128** — float audio outside ±1.0.

## Root cause

Against the ffmpeg reference the buffer is not a different mix, not shifted (best lag 0), not distorted. Least-squares fit:

```
best-fit gain = 1.4140  = √2
residual after scaling = 0.6   (reference RMS 2578.8)
```

Exactly right audio, √2 too loud.

`libswresample`'s `rematrix_maxval` default is **format-dependent**: 1.0 for integer output, **unbounded for float**. So a stereo → mono downmix to FLTP uses energy-preserving coefficients (1/√2 per channel) instead of amplitude-preserving ones (1/2). Reasonable for a chain that normalizes later; a trap for one feeding a model trained on ±1.0 audio.

## Causal, not correlated

Feeding whisper the **correct** audio scaled by √2 reproduces the failure exactly:

| audio | unique lines | worst repeat |
|---|---|---|
| reference | 869 | 57 |
| reference × √2 | 283 | **1,238** |

1,238 against the 1,236 originally observed. Gain is the whole cause.

## The change

`ResamplerOptions` gains `RematrixMaxval` (0 = library default, so **no behaviour change for existing callers**); `whisper_stt` sets 1.0. Verified: peak 1.3128 → 0.9283, and the buffer now matches the ffmpeg reference at gain 0.9998, residual 0.74.

## Tests

- `TestResamplerDownmixNormalization` pins the contract, and *skips with a message* rather than failing if a future libswresample starts capping float by default — so the option's rationale gets revisited instead of silently rotting.
- `TestWhisperSTTResampleDiag` is kept, env-gated (`MM_DIAG_AUDIO`), skipping by default. It is what turned three plausible suspects into one measurement, and the failure mode it catches is silent: correct length, correct content, wrong scale, no error anywhere.
- `av` suite green; `processors` green under `-run Whisper`. Note `TestTwelveLabs*` fails on clean `main` too — pre-existing, unrelated.

title: feat(av): survive structurally corrupt packets from damaged containers
body:
## Why

A demuxer driven by a malformed container (lying PES lengths, non-interleaved AVI, truncated tape captures) can report a *successful* read yet leave the `AVPacket` structurally inconsistent. The next `av_packet_unref` / `av_packet_free` dereferences the poison and takes the **whole process** down with an access violation — a fatal fault no caller can catch (in a Go host, a cgo access violation is not a recoverable panic). Observed in the wild: a fatal fault inside `av_packet_unref` during a keyframe scan of damaged M2TS / DV-AVI captures, right after `[mpegts] PES packet size mismatch / Packet corrupt` warnings.

The demux idiom (`pkt.Unref(); ReadPacket(pkt)`) is the public API surface, so the hardening lands **in the binding**, where every caller — host applications included — inherits it.

## What

- **`mm_packet_guard.c/.h`** — consistency check (poisoned/misaligned pointers, impossible size, side-data disagreement), *scrub* (abandon references without touching them: one leaked buffer per damaged file beats a dead process), guarded unref/free, and a guarded `av_read_frame` that validates the packet **and its stream_index** after every successful read.
- **`Packet.Unref` / `Packet.Close`** route through the guards (`av_packet_free` unrefs internally, so an unguarded Close dies on the same poison). `ScrubbedPacketCount()` reports how often the guard fired so hosts can quarantine the offending media. `Packet.IsCorrupt()` surfaces `AV_PKT_FLAG_CORRUPT`.
- **`ReadPacket`** returns a typed `ErrPoisonedPacket` (abandon the input) instead of leaving a live grenade for the next iteration.
- **`ForEachPacket`** — one owned demux loop: alloc/unref/close handled internally, payload-corrupt packets skipped, `ErrStopDemux` for early exit. Callers can no longer get the reuse discipline wrong.
- **`OpenInputResilient`** — damaged-media profile for analysis/scanning paths: `fflags +discardcorrupt`, bounded probing (16 MiB / 10 s), and an interrupt-callback watchdog (30 s open budget; per-read deadline via `SetReadDeadline`, surfacing `IsInterrupted`) so a demuxer wedged by damaged input returns an error instead of hanging its caller forever. Well-formed files behave identically; remux/copy paths should keep plain `OpenInput`.

## Tests

- Reproduce the observed crash signature (all-ones pointers, negative size) against guarded `Unref` and `Close` — with a bare `av_packet_unref` these lines are a process death, not a test failure.
- Drive real mpegts/AVI demuxers over deterministically damaged fixtures (truncation, scribbled header region, scribbled middle, spread bit flips) with both open flavours and both loop styles; the fixtures provoke genuine `Packet corrupt` demuxer states. Contract: any outcome is acceptable except death.
- Watchdog: an expired read deadline fails with `IsInterrupted` long before EOF.
- `go test ./...` and `go test -race ./av` green.

## Honest limits (also in the file comments)

A dangling-but-plausible pointer is indistinguishable from a live one without dereferencing it — which is the crash being avoided. This guard stops scribbled/poisoned structs; it is defence in depth, not a proof of safety. For input that corrupts the demuxer's own heap, process isolation (one file, one worker process) remains the complete answer and is deliberately out of scope here.

title: fix(processors): SequenceEditor use-after-free — frame cloned after handoff to the encoder node
body:
## The race

`SequenceEditor.render` emits each composited frame via `emitVideo`, which sends it across a channel to the **encoder node's goroutine** — and that goroutine `Close()`s the frame once it's encoded (`job/handlers_encoder.go`). The editor then took its hold/freeze clone **after** the send:

```go
if err := emitVideo(outFrame); err != nil { ... }
...
if cl, cerr := outFrame.Clone(); cerr == nil {   // races the encoder's free
    se.lastFrame = cl
}
```

With the scheduler's buffered edges the clone usually wins; on a contended machine the encoder dequeues and frees first, and `av_frame_clone` reads a freed `AVFrame` — an intermittent access violation (0xc0000005 on Windows, SIGSEGV elsewhere), or a `-race` report between `Frame.Close`'s free and the clone's read.

## The fix — delete the clone, not reorder it

`se.lastFrame` turns out to be **write-only**: nothing in the repo reads it. Gap/freeze holds are actually served by the clip readers (each holds its own previous frame on EAGAIN). So the clone was pure overhead — one `av_frame_clone` per output frame — carrying a use-after-free. Removed the field, its `Close()` cleanup, and the post-emit clone; the ownership rule is now stated at the emit site: **nothing may touch a frame after a successful send.**

## Validation

- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./processors/` clean.
- All `Sequence*` processor tests pass.
- A 2-clip end-to-end graph render (sequence → scale → encoder) is race-clean under `-race`, repeated. (The two pre-existing `processors` test failures on this machine — MetadataWriter/TwelveLabs — fail identically on `main`; unrelated.)

title: feat(av): FlushBuffers on HWDecoderContext
body:
Seeked multi-frame extraction — decode a set of timestamps through one demuxer open — needs the post-seek decoder reset (`avcodec_flush_buffers`) on hardware decoders too. `DecoderContext` has `FlushBuffers`; `HWDecoderContext` only had `Flush` (the drain/EOF signal, which leaves the decoder refusing packets — the exact confusion the software twin's test guards). This adds the mirror method so seek-and-decode loops can drive either decoder through one interface.

`TestHWDecoderFlushBuffersAllowsDecodeAfterSeek` is the hardware twin of the existing software test: probes available device types (VideoToolbox → CUDA → VAAPI → QSV), skips where none opens (CI runners), and where one does — verified live on Apple silicon VideoToolbox — decodes, seeks, resets with FlushBuffers, and decodes again, asserting AutoTransfer returns software frames throughout. Uses the existing optional `testdata/tiny.mp4` fixture convention (skip when absent).

title: feat(face): optional facial-expression assessment — blendshapes, smile + eyes-open
body:
## What

Optional facial-expression assessment in the `face` package: `AssessFaceExpression(img, bbox, landmarks)` returns 52 ARKit-compatible blendshape coefficients plus two derived headline scores — **Smile** and **EyesOpen**, both continuous in [0,1] — for a detected face. Host applications can rank, gate, or search with the scores; the full coefficient vector is exposed for downstream uses.

Follows the visibility model's pattern exactly: **optional** and **lazy** — two more ONNX sessions built on first use, both-or-neither; bundles without the models keep full detect/embed/visibility capability (`ExpressionAvailable()` reports the reason); failed init is not cached, so fetching the models later recovers without a restart. CPU-pinned and deterministic.

## Models

MediaPipe Face Landmarker's dense-landmark + blendshape cascade (Google; **Apache-2.0 per the FaceMesh V2 and Blendshape V2 model cards**), converted TFLite → ONNX and hosted as the [`face-expression-model-v1`](https://github.com/MediaMolder/mediamolder/releases/tag/face-expression-model-v1) release assets (Google publishes only the bundled `.task`; float16 is the only precision it ships — it is what the upstream runtime executes too).

- `face_landmarks_detector.onnx`: 256×256 eye-aligned face crop → 478×(x,y,z) landmarks + a face-presence logit. A third model output (tongue-out) is not bound — the upstream pipeline drops it as well.
- `face_blendshapes.onnx`: a fixed 146-landmark subset (x,y) → 52 coefficients. Per its model card the model "encapsulates all necessary scale, rotation and translation normalizations", so the mesh's crop-space coordinates feed it directly — no re-projection.

`scripts/convert-expression-models.sh` is the reproducible recipe with full provenance (source URL + sha, member shas, tooling pins). One honest caveat it documents: **tf2onnx's graph emission is not byte-deterministic** (its transpose-optimizer order follows Python object identity; re-runs even produce ±4 Reshape/Transpose nodes), so unlike the visibility recipe the script verifies **numeric equivalence against the TFLite source** on seeded probes (mesh max|Δ| < 2e-3, blendshapes < 1e-4) instead of a byte hash; the release assets are the pinned artifacts of record, SHA-256-verified at load like every other model.

## Mechanics

- Crop: square window centred on the bbox, side 1.5×max(w,h) (the upstream ROI expansion), rotated so the detector's eye line runs horizontal; nearest-neighbour, black out-of-bounds padding, pure Go, deterministic. Degenerate/absent landmarks fall back to axis-aligned.
- Presence gate: the landmark model's face-presence logit (sigmoid, threshold 0.5) — below it the call returns `ErrNoFace` rather than hallucinated coefficients (heavy occlusion, stale bbox, false-positive detection).
- `Smile = mean(mouthSmileLeft/Right)`, `EyesOpen = 1 − mean(eyeBlinkLeft/Right)`.
- New: `DefaultExpressionMeshSpec` / `DefaultExpressionBlendshapesSpec` / `CheckExpressionModels` (separate from `CheckModels`, the `CheckVisibilityModel` stance); `BlendshapeNames` + index constants; fetch script section for the two release assets.

## Validation

- Unit tests (no ONNX needed): crop geometry + rotation, sampler determinism and padding, subset extraction, score derivation, table pinning (146 ascending in-range indices; names at the 4 used indices).
- TFLite↔ONNX numeric parity on seeded probes (in the convert script, run against these exact assets): mesh 3.7e-4, presence 8.6e-6, blendshapes 7.8e-7.
- `TestExpressionIntegration` (env-gated like the others): real photos through detect → expression, determinism + range + presence asserts. Semantic spot-checks on public-domain portraits:

| fixture | presence | smile | eyesOpen |
|---|---|---|---|
| broad smile, eyes open | 1.000 | **0.939** | 0.719 |
| neutral, eyes open | 1.000 | **0.000** | **0.932** |
| smiling, eyes shut | 1.000 | 0.730 | **0.209** |

- Fetch script verified end-to-end against the published release; full `face` suite green under both build configs (`go test ./face/`, `go test -tags with_onnx ./face/` with models + fixture), `-race` clean, `go build ./...` clean.

title: face: visibility (occlusion) assessment — measure how much of a face is covered
body:
## What

`face.AssessFaceVisibility(img, bbox) (float32, error)` — the fraction of a detected face covered by something in front of it (a hand, a raised glass, another person's shoulder), in [0,1]. **Measured, not inferred**: a portrait multiclass-segmentation model labels a head-context crop; inside the (10%-shrunk) face box, anything that is not `face-skin` or `hair` is coverage — a hand reads as `body-skin`, a cup as `other`, whatever the occluder is. Calibrated so a clean tight detector box (~85% skin+hair) reads 0.

## Design points

- **Optional + lazy.** A third session on the shared pipeline, built on first use: bundles without the model keep full detect/embed capability (`Capable()` unchanged), `VisibilityAvailable()`/`CheckVisibilityModel(dir)` report its own state, and failed init is not cached (the `ensurePipeline` convention). Default builds return `ErrUnsupported` like the rest of the seam.
- **Deterministic.** CPU provider, nearest-neighbour letterbox geometry (`letterboxGeom` pinned bit-identical to `letterbox` by test), argmax on logits — same input, same fraction, every machine.
- **Model + licensing.** MediaPipe Multiclass Segmentation (Google) — **Apache-2.0 per its model card**, trained on Google's own data. Converted TFLite→ONNX (NCHW input): `scripts/convert-visibility-model.sh` is the reproducible recipe with full provenance (source sha, tooling versions, output sha); the artifact is hosted as the [`face-visibility-model-v1`](https://github.com/MediaMolder/MediaMolder/releases/tag/face-visibility-model-v1) release asset (Google publishes only the TFLite) and `fetch-face-models.sh` pin-verifies it end-to-end (verified).

## Verification

- Pure math: `occlusionFromMask` semantics (hair = hairstyle not occluder; body-skin = coverage; expected-cover calibration; degenerate regions), context/measure rect geometry incl. frame-edge clamping, `letterboxGeom == letterbox` across shapes.
- Stub contract: `ErrUnsupported`, zero value.
- Env-gated integration (real models + runtime, run locally): 9 detected faces in a face-grid fixture all assess **0.000** deterministically; painting a 55% synthetic occluder over one face moves it to **0.474** — matching the calibration math (1 − 0.45/0.85 ≈ 0.47).
- Default + `with_onnx` builds, vet, and the full face suite green in both configurations.

title: ci: retry FFmpeg download and fall back to a mirror
body:
## Why

Run [30208658310](https://github.com/MediaMolder/mediamolder/actions/runs/30208658310) failed on `main` in the GUI build job — not a code issue:

```
curl: (28) Failed to connect to ffmpeg.org port 443 after 135927 ms: Couldn't connect to server
xz: (stdin): File format not recognized
tar: Child returned status 1
```

The download step piped `curl` straight into `tar`, so a single ffmpeg.org outage killed the build with no retry and no fallback.

## What

At all five FFmpeg-from-source sites (Linux, macOS, ASan, Lint, GUI):

- `curl` now retries (`--retry 5 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 5 --connect-timeout 30`) and downloads to a file before extracting, instead of streaming into `tar`.
- On failure, fall back to the GitHub tag tarball (`FFmpeg/FFmpeg` `n${FFMPEG_VERSION}`), normalising the extracted directory name back to `ffmpeg-${FFMPEG_VERSION}` so the following `cd` and `./configure` are unchanged.

No version or build-flag changes. YAML validated.

title: feat(face): no-reference sharpness + exposure on the aligned crop
body:
Two bounded [0,1] no-reference quality metrics on the face API, for ranking a subject's own faces.

- **Sharpness** — log-scaled variance-of-Laplacian of the luma (focus).
- **Exposure** — mid-gray-peaked mean luma, penalized by the clipped-pixel fraction (light level).

Both computed on the same 112×112 aligned crop the embedder already produces, so they cost ~nothing at embed time (`analyzeImage`, behind `with_onnx`). `Face` gains `Sharpness`/`Exposure`.

`AssessFace(img, landmarks) Metrics` re-aligns from the stored 5-point landmarks and measures **without** re-detecting or re-embedding — pure Go, no model dependency — so a caller can backfill faces detected before these metrics existed.

Deliberately **not** the full frame-quality work in `docs/architecture/proposals/blur-detection.md`; just a stable focus + exposure score. `sharpnessRef` only affects the [0,1] spread, not the ordering (log is monotonic in variance).

Builds clean default + `with_onnx`; tests cover flat-vs-checker sharpness ordering, mid-gray-vs-clipped exposure, and AssessFace on textured input.

title: Frame-accurate smart copy: trim without re-encoding the interior
body:
Trimming a graph today forces a choice: stream-copy and land on the nearest
keyframe (off by up to a GOP), or re-encode the whole stream and lose a
generation. This branch adds a third option — re-encode only the boundary,
copy everything else byte-for-byte.

## Video — `codec_video: "smartcopy"`

A new `graph.KindSmartCopy` node sits between source and sink. It classifies
GOPs against the trim window, copies whole interior GOPs verbatim, and decodes
+ re-encodes only the GOP(s) the cut points land in. Boundary decode is primed
with the previous GOP so open-GOP references resolve. Target inherits the
source codec, size, frame rate, pixel format, SAR, profile/level and bit rate.

Supporting changes: the source stays a plain demuxer forwarding the raw
bitstream; the sink registers via `AddStreamFromInput` (extradata from source)
and skips output-timing on the smartcopy channel; a smartcopy output never
fires a global `-to` stop, so the tail GOP can complete.

## Audio — sample-accurate on both paths

- **Re-encoded audio** (`spliceAudioTrimForOutputs`): inserts an `atrim` in
  front of the audio encoder, mirroring FFmpeg's `insert_trim` in fftools.
  Cuts now land on the exact sample rather than the nearest packet —
  previously off by up to ~21 ms per edge. No `asetpts`; the sink's existing
  shift-to-zero handles rebasing.
- **PCM** (`codec_audio: "smartcopy"`): a per-packet (not per-GOP) state
  machine copies interior packets verbatim and byte-slices the packets
  straddling each edge to the exact sample. No decode, no encoder priming, no
  container edit-list surgery — lossless and sample-exact.

Compressed audio (AAC/FLAC/Opus/…) is rejected with an error pointing at
`codec_audio: <encoder>` or `codec_audio: "copy"`. Seamless boundary
re-encode there needs per-codec priming and gapless handling (pre-skip, edit
lists) and is deferred.

## GUI

"Smart copy (video)" and "Smart copy (audio, PCM)" palette entries, each with
a dedicated properties panel. The video panel exposes the full boundary
encoder (rate control, preset, tune, profile/level, raw x264/x265-params) plus
a boundary-encoder override and global-header toggle. The audio panel is a
no-parameter info panel — PCM slicing has no encoder. The trim window lives on
the connected output's Timing section, since it applies to every stream.

Round-trip: `expandImplicitEncoders` skips explicit smartcopy nodes so
GUI-authored graphs aren't re-wrapped, and a new `stampSmartCopyTiming` pass
copies the window from the output options onto explicit nodes.

## Testing

- `job/handlers_smartcopy_test.go` — interior packets byte-identical to the
  source on an open-GOP input; only boundary GOPs re-encoded.
- `job/smart_audio_copy_test.go` — a fractional-second PCM trim is bit-for-bit
  equal to the source sample sub-range.
- `job/audio_trim_test.go` — re-encoded audio trim lands within ~13 ms
  (sub-frame) of the requested window on the BBB fixture.
- `TestSmartCopyExplicitNode` — GUI-shaped graph (explicit node, window in
  output options, codec shorthand stripped) produces a byte-identical interior.
- `testdata/examples/67_smartcopy_trim.json` runs end-to-end in
  `TestExamplesRun`.

`go build ./...` and `go test ./...` are clean.

## Docs

New `docs/smartcopy.md`; updates to `README.md`, `docs/gui.md`,
`docs/json-config-reference.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`. Embedded GUI assets rebuilt
via `make build-gui-static`.

## Also included

`chore(deps)` bumping the golang.org/x modules, which also restores `go.sum`
`/go.mod` hash lines that had gone missing and broke the build.

title: fix(av): VideoToolbox encoders fall back to software when no HW session
body:
## Problem

VideoToolbox encoders (`h264_videotoolbox`, `hevc_videotoolbox`, `prores_videotoolbox`) default to **hardware-only** (`allow_sw=0`). On any host without a usable hardware encode session — a headless/virtualized macOS CI runner, or a machine whose HW encoder is absent or busy — `avcodec_open2` hard-fails:

```
[h264_videotoolbox] Cannot create compression session: -12903
Try -allow_sw 1. The hardware encoder may be busy, or not supported.
avcodec_open2(h264_videotoolbox): averror(-542398533): Generic error in an external library
```

Every video-encoding path (transcode, trim, slideshow render, frame extraction) then fails on such hosts.

## Fix

`OpenEncoder` now defaults `allow_sw=1` for any `*_videotoolbox` codec (unless the caller set it explicitly). VideoToolbox still prefers hardware where present and only uses its software encoder when no hardware session can be created — encode degrades in speed rather than failing outright. This is FFmpeg's own documented remedy (`Try -allow_sw 1`).

## Verification

- New darwin test `TestVideoToolboxEncoderOpensViaSoftware`: opens the encoder via the forced-software path (`require_sw=1`) and via default options, confirming the software fallback target is viable and the default opens on a HW-less host. Passes locally.
- Full `av` package + `go vet` green; no regression to the hardware path.
- The fix is a no-op for non-VideoToolbox encoders (libx264 etc.).

title: Feat/av tile grid
body:
Grid-coded HEIF-family stills — smartphone HEICs store a 4032×3024 photo as 48 independently-coded 512×512 HEVC tiles, and grid AVIFs use the same layout — describe their true geometry in an `AV_STREAM_GROUP_PARAMS_TILE_GRID` stream group. A decode loop that picks "the" video stream renders a single tile. This PR exposes the group so hosts can compose the real image.

## New surface

- **`(*InputFormatContext).TileGrids() []TileGridInfo`** — canvas (`CodedWidth`/`CodedHeight`), presentation crop window (`Width`/`Height` at `HorizontalOffset`/`VerticalOffset`), `Background` RGBA, and composition-ordered `Tiles`. Each tile is mapped to its **container-level** stream index (libavformat's `offsets[].idx` indexes the group's own stream list; the binding resolves it so tiles plug straight into `OpenDecoder`). `Default` carries `AV_DISPOSITION_DEFAULT` so hosts can prefer the container's primary item when a file also carries auxiliary grids (gain map, depth images are grids too).
- A malformed `offsets[].idx` (header-contract violation / corrupt metadata) drops the **whole group** rather than one tile — a grid missing a tile would compose a valid-looking image with a background hole, silent corruption a caller can't detect; returning no grid makes callers fall back to their existing single-stream behavior.
- `StreamInfo`'s doc comment now cross-references `TileGrids` — the whole bug class is "picked a stream, ignored the group", and the warning belongs where decode-loop authors already look.

## Tests

- **Always-on:** `TestTileGridsNonGrid` opens a synthetic lavfi input and asserts `TileGrids() == nil`, so the cgo path (stream-group reads) executes in every CI leg with no fixture.
- **Env-gated:** `TestTileGridsHEIF` (`HEIF_GRID_TEST_FILE=<path>`) verifies the full contract against a real 48-tile smartphone HEIC — canvas/crop invariants, every tile strictly inside the canvas, container-level stream indexes valid and video-typed, and the presentation image larger than any single tile. Grid fixtures are personal photos, so none is checked in.

## Notes

- `main` is merged in, so this applies cleanly on top of the LibRaw/mingw work.
- No behavior change for existing callers; the API is additive and present on all platforms at the package's FFmpeg 8.1 floor (stream groups are unconditional there). `go vet` + the full `av` suite green, verified on windows/amd64 against FFmpeg 8.1.

title: feat(raw): LibRaw builds on Windows/mingw — static, self-contained link
body:
LibRaw 0.21.3 now builds and links on windows/amd64 under the MSYS2 mingw toolchain — the `raw` package (`with_libraw`) was previously darwin/linux-only.

## Changes

- **`raw/cgo_flags_libraw.go`** — a `windows` LDFLAGS branch: `-static-libgcc -Wl,-Bstatic -lstdc++ -lz -lwinpthread -Wl,-Bdynamic -lm -lws2_32`. The `-Wl,-Bstatic` window is load-bearing: plain `-lstdc++`/`-lz` resolve to MinGW **import** libs, leaving the binary dependent on `libstdc++-6.dll`/`zlib1.dll` — dead on any machine without MSYS2's bin dir on PATH (verified by objdump before/after). `-lws2_32` covers LibRaw's winsock references (a system DLL). gcc's implicit trailing `-lpthread` still imports `libwinpthread-1.dll` — accepted and documented: the `av` package's libav DLLs make a Windows binary dynamic regardless, and host applications that bundle mediamolder already stage the transitive DLL closure (objdump -p), which carries winpthread automatically.
- **`scripts/bundle-libraw.sh`** — `sha256sum` fallback (MSYS2/Git Bash ship no `shasum`); warns when run from the plain-MSYS shell (a cygwin-CRT archive fails the later cgo link with cryptic `__imp_*` errors); header no longer claims the fixed `-lraw -lc++ -lz` flag set. The existing non-Darwin branch handles the mingw configure/make unchanged.
- **`scripts/fetch-face-models.sh`** — the same `sha256sum` fallback (it had the identical `shasum`-only failure mode on Windows).
- **Docs** — `docs/build/windows.md` §raw_decode names the MinGW64 shell and scopes the "no runtime DLL" claim to LibRaw itself; `docs/architecture/raw-decode.md` documents the per-platform link flags and adds Windows to the reproducibility-coverage note.

## Verification

Built under MSYS2 MINGW64: LibRaw 0.21.3 configure/make/install from the SHA-256-pinned tarball; `go vet`/`go test -tags with_libraw ./raw/...` green on windows/amd64; objdump on the test exe shows **no** `libstdc++-6.dll`/`zlib1.dll` imports. A downstream host's full-tag build against this checkout confirms RAW capability end-to-end.

No API changes and no pin-bump requirement for module consumers: the static lib lives in the checkout's git-ignored `third_party/` (published modules never carry it), so this only affects `with_libraw` builds made against a checkout.

title: feat(face): add CoreML execution provider (opt-in, Apple silicon)
body:
MEDIAMOLDER_FACE_EP=coreml routes YOLOv8-face + SFace onto CoreML (AppendExecutionProviderCoreMLV2, MLComputeUnits=ALL) — the Apple Neural Engine / GPU on Apple silicon — and falls back cleanly to CPU on any runtime without the CoreML provider (non-Apple platforms, CPU-only builds).

CoreML is opt-in only, deliberately NOT in the auto order: its reduced-precision Neural-Engine/GPU path can shift SFace embeddings slightly from the CPU path, so a host enables it explicitly once it has confirmed downstream use (clustering, dedup) tolerates that. With MEDIAMOLDER_FACE_EP unset, an Apple-silicon host stays on the deterministic CPU provider — behavior is byte-identical to before.

Extracts the EnvFaceEP -> provider-order routing into a pure providersFor() helper so the opt-in invariant is unit-tested (TestProvidersFor) without the ONNX runtime.

title: feat(raw): high-precision 16-bit linear wide-gamut develop (DecodeDevelop)
body:
## Summary
Adds a high-precision RAW develop — `DecodeDevelop` — alongside the existing 8-bit `Decode`, for downstream consumers needing a high-precision, wide-gamut, colour-managed display/export pipeline.

`Decode` returns the canonical **8-bit sRGB** raster (used for pixel hashing). `DecodeDevelop` returns a **scene-referred master**:
- **16-bit** `*image.NRGBA64` (`output_bps=16`) — genuine precision, not 8-bit widened
- **linear light** (`gamm={1,1}`) — no transfer curve baked; the consumer tone-maps in float
- **wide gamut** — Rec.2020 (`output_color=8`), reported via `ColorSpace`
- **highlights recovered** (`highlight=2` blend) vs the 8-bit path's clip (`highlight=0`)
- un-oriented, opaque, deterministic; carries a `DevelopVersion` for cache keying

Demosaic (AHD), white balance (camera) and orientation (`user_flip=0`) match the 8-bit path. Build-tagged exactly like `Decode` (stub errors cleanly in the default build); the 8-bit `Decode` and its tests are untouched.

## Verification
- `with_libraw`: develops the DNG fixture to a non-uniform 16-bit `NRGBA64` — **3069/3072 px carry sub-8-bit detail** (proves true 16-bit), in Rec.2020.
- Default (stub) build + existing `raw` tests unaffected.

title: fix(security): harden path-injection & allocation sinks (CodeQL)
body:
## Harden network-reachable path-injection / allocation sinks

Triage + fixes for the 7 open CodeQL **high** alerts on the code-scanning page. Each was assessed by trust boundary; this PR fixes the genuinely network-reachable / fixable ones and documents the rest.

### Triage of all 7 alerts

| # | Rule | Location | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| **#49** | `go/path-injection` | `internal/distributed/orchestrator/orchestrator.go` | **Real** — fixed |
| **#33** | `go/uncontrolled-allocation-size` | `runtime/scheduler.go` | **Real** — fixed |
| **#11/#12** | `go/path-injection` | `internal/gui/files.go` (`handleMkdir`) | False-positive (guarded), but fixed for consistency + to clear the alert |
| **#6/#7/#8** | `go/path-injection` | `av/mux.go` (`os.Rename`/`os.Remove`) | By-design at the sink — documented, follow-up below |

### Fixes

**`orchestrator` (#49) — arbitrary file read.** `materializeFanoutDynamic` read a fanout manifest from a job-supplied `manifest_uri` via `os.ReadFile` of *any* absolute path; the `//nolint:gosec` only checked `IsAbs`, so a submitted job could read e.g. `file:///etc/passwd`. Now confined to operator-approved roots (the server's `AllowedRoots`, or a safe default of temp-dir + cwd when none are set), passing the **re-derived** path to the FS. The worker reaches this path too (single-binary Phase B), so the default keeps it safe without new CLI flags.

**`runtime` (#33) — allocation DoS.** Each edge channel was sized from an `EdgeBufSizes` hint derived from the (possibly remote/untrusted) `ExecutionPlan`, unbounded — a job could request an arbitrarily large `make(chan any, N)`. Now clamped to `maxEdgeBuffer` (65536, far beyond any real pipeline).

**`gui` (#11/#12) — handleMkdir.** Was guarded by a boolean `isWithinAnyRoot` check (functionally safe, but not a CodeQL sanitizer) then operated on the raw path. Switched to the existing `sanitizePathAnyRoot` (returns a value re-derived from the matched root), matching the other file handlers; removed the now-dead `isWithinAnyRoot`/`isWithinRoot`. The GUI browser is intentionally filesystem-wide for local use — this is a consistency + static-analysis fix, not a new restriction.

### Not changed here — `av/mux.go` (#6/#7/#8)

The flagged `os.Rename`/`os.Remove` are the **core muxer** writing the job's output file. Confining them in `av` would break legitimate local writes (the CLI's whole purpose), and the muxer has no trust boundary of its own. The right place to gate a remote job's **output** path is the server, which today validates file:// **inputs** (`checkAllowedPaths`) but not outputs. Recommended follow-up: extend output-path validation at the `serve` boundary (carefully — the orchestrator rewrites outputs to storage-scoped URIs via `segmentOutputURI`). Left out of this PR to keep it focused and avoid touching distributed output semantics without dedicated testing.

### Tests
- `orchestrator`: `confineToRoots` + `readManifestFile` reject `/etc/passwd`, relative, and no-roots; accept within-root; existing fanout tests still pass via the safe default.
- `runtime`: `clampEdgeBuffer` bounds huge hints.
- `gui`: `handleMkdir` creates within a root and rejects non-component names.

Default `go build ./...` + affected-package tests green; `gofmt -s`/`go vet` clean. Independent of the LibRaw work.
