title: feat(raw): camera-RAW decoding via bundled LibRaw
body:
## Camera-RAW decoding via LibRaw

MediaMolder's only image path is libav, which renders camera RAW (NEF/CR2/CR3/ARW/RAF/ORF/RW2/PEF/SRW/DNG) to a **black/garbled frame** — it's a codec library, not a develop pipeline (no CFA demosaic, no white balance). This adds a `raw` package that develops camera RAW to a full, demosaicked **8-bit sRGB** raster via bundled, version-pinned **LibRaw** (the field standard used by digiKam/Krita/ImageMagick), mirroring the `face` package's optional-native-dependency boundary.

Gated behind `//go:build with_libraw` with a pure-Go `!with_libraw` stub, so **the default build is byte-for-byte unaffected**.

### What's included
- **`raw` package** — frozen API `Capable()` / `IsRAW()` / `Decode()` / `ErrUnsupported`; cgo LibRaw decoder under a fixed, deterministic parameter set (camera WB, sRGB, AHD demosaic, no auto-brightness, `user_flip=0` so orientation stays caller-owned); recovers cgo panics into errors.
- **`raw_decode` graph node** — a FrameSource `go_processor` that develops one RAW into a full-res RGBA frame for the graph (scale/encode/export a real develop).
- **CLI** — `mediamolder raw-decode` (→ PNG/JPEG) and a `raw-setup` doctor.
- **GUI** — `GET /api/raw-capabilities`, palette entry + Inspector form with a "no LibRaw" banner; embedded `dist` regenerated.
- **Build/bundle** — `scripts/bundle-libraw.sh` builds a SHA-256-pinned **static** LibRaw 0.21.3 from source into `third_party/libraw` (gitignored; we ship no binary), universal arm64+x86_64 on macOS, with the CDDL-1.0 license bundled. Makefile: `bundle-libraw` / `build-libraw` / `test-libraw` / `build-gui-libraw` (composes via `EXTRA_TAGS`).
- **CI** — a gated `libraw` leg (no FFmpeg needed; bundles LibRaw and runs the decode/determinism tests); the default leg stays on the stub and green.
- **Docs** — user guide, architecture design doc, build-and-packaging + macOS/Linux/Windows build pages, README, CHANGELOG.

### Design decisions
- **Explicit develop only** — a `raw_decode` node + CLI; no transparent auto-develop at the source node, so **no schema / `jobTypes` churn**. The transparent path is documented as a deferred Phase 2.
- **Static link** — bundled `libraw.a` (no runtime dylib/rpath), the whisper/x264 pattern rather than ONNX's dlopen. `Capable()` reflects the build tag; the SHA-256 pin is verified at bundle time.
- **Determinism, scoped** — reproducible per platform + pinned version; cross-arch identity is recorded, not load-bearing (dedup/preview hashing never touches LibRaw).
- **Fixture** — `raw/testdata/sample.dng` is a self-authored **CC0** RGGB-Bayer DNG with its generator committed alongside.

### Verification
- **`with_libraw`:** built real LibRaw 0.21.3; decoded the fixture to a non-uniform, deterministic, landscape (`user_flip=0`) sRGB raster; `go build ./...` + `raw`/`processors`/`internal/gui` tests pass; the CLI wrote valid 64×48 PNGs; `raw-setup` → ✅, `list-processors` shows `raw_decode`.
- **Default (stub):** `go build ./...` + tests green; `raw-setup`/`raw-decode` give actionable errors (no crash); `raw_decode` absent from the catalog.
- The bundle script's macOS universal+`lipo` path was validated from scratch.

### Notes
- The `raw` package source is LGPL-headed like the repo; the linked GPL FFmpeg already governs the combined binary's license (unchanged here).
- Pre-existing and untouched: `cmd/mediamolder/cmd_go_scene_detect.go` isn't `gofmt -s`-clean in the base.

title: fix(ci): install ffmpeg CLI so the BBB transcode runs in CI
body:
## Summary
**Fixes a CI regression on `main`.** Every `build-and-test` matrix job + `asan` are red because the **"Fetch BBB testdata source"** step fails with `error: ffmpeg not found on PATH`.

### Root cause
`scripts/fetch-bbb.sh` (changed in #43) transcodes the Blender source to H.264/AAC using the **`ffmpeg` CLI**. But CI builds FFmpeg with `--disable-programs` — it produces only the **libraries** (which MediaMolder links via cgo), **no `ffmpeg` binary**. So the transcode step fails on every job, and since #43 merged, `main` itself is red.

### Fix
- Install the apt **`ffmpeg`** package on the Linux `build-and-test` and `asan` jobs (independent of the source-built libs — used only to prepare test data; its different soname can't shadow the `/usr/local` FFmpeg 8.1 libs).
- **Gate the BBB fetch to Linux.** Only the Linux-only example/community suite needs the H.264 source; the `aspect`/`metadata` e2e tests `t.Skip` gracefully when it's absent. So macOS no longer needs the CLI and stops failing on it (those e2e tests remain covered on the Linux jobs).

### Why not download a pre-encoded H.264 file instead?
The only ready 1080p H.264 BBB (Blender's `…_h264.mov`) is **692 MB with 5.1 audio + a data stream** — it diverges from the validated **stereo** test data and would risk the audio/stream-mapping examples. Keeping the deterministic transcode reproduces the exact fixture the suite was validated against.

### Validation
- YAML parses; 4 jobs intact; BBB gating applied to `build-and-test` only (asan stays ungated — it's Linux-only and now has the CLI).
- `fetch-bbb.sh` is unchanged and was validated locally (full example+community suite green against the transcoded file).

### Follow-ups
Once merged, the open PRs branched off `main` (#42 native-faces, #44 LFS cache) just need a rebase to pick this up and go green.

title: ci: shrink CI caches — scope FFmpeg cache + cache LFS objects
body:
## Summary
Two cache changes that cut LFS bandwidth **and** CI wall-clock for this (public) repo.

### 1. Scope the FFmpeg cache to its own artefacts
The four Linux jobs cached the **entire `/usr/local` tree** — multiple GB of preinstalled runner tooling — so every run spent minutes in the **"Post Cache FFmpeg"** save step uploading data unrelated to FFmpeg (this is the long cache-save you can see at the tail of recent runs). Now they cache only what the source build installs:

```
/usr/local/lib/libav*  /usr/local/lib/libsw*  /usr/local/lib/libpostproc*
/usr/local/lib/pkgconfig/lib*.pc
/usr/local/include/{libav*,libsw*,libpostproc*}
```

Build/linker/pkg-config behaviour is unchanged — FFmpeg still installs to `/usr/local`, so the `.pc` prefixes stay valid; only *what gets cached* shrinks. Keys are bumped so a fresh small cache replaces the bloated one. macOS already scopes to `/usr/local/ffmpeg` and is untouched.

*First run per bumped key is a normal cache miss → rebuilds FFmpeg exactly as before → then saves the small cache. Subsequent runs restore fast.*

### 2. Cache Git LFS objects; skip LFS pull in lint/gui
`build-and-test` (×4 matrix) + `asan` ran `git lfs pull` every run, re-downloading the ~9 MB fixture set against GitHub's free 1 GB/month LFS bandwidth. Cache `.git/lfs` keyed on the object oids so a pull only hits the network when a fixture changes. `lint`/`gui` build-only — make their checkout explicitly `lfs: false`.

## Validation
- YAML parses; all four Linux FFmpeg caches scoped (macOS unchanged); LFS cache shared OS-independently.
- No production code; CI config only.

A go_processor that runs the [Whisper](https://github.com/openai/whisper), a general purpose speech recognition model from OpenAI. The whisper node transcribes an audio stream to timestamped text locally with[whisper.cpp](https://github.com/ggml-org/whisper.cpp) — offline, no network — gated behind the with_whisper build tag. We ship neither libwhisper nor any model; users supply both.

title: fix(gui): bound directory listing; cache volume enumeration
body:
The GUI file dialog could hang the whole server: GET /api/files ran os.ReadDir/os.Stat/DirEntry.Info and re-walked /Volumes (via defaultRoots -> shortcutRoots/localDrives) on every request with no timeout. A slow or stale mount — a sleeping external drive, a disconnected share — left those non-cancellable syscalls blocked forever, wedging the file picker and stalling the server's graceful shutdown (Ctrl-C appeared dead because the in-flight request never returned).

Run the listing under a 5s bound via callWithTimeout: on timeout the request returns 504 and the blocked goroutine is abandoned (it no longer holds the connection), so the server stays responsive and can shut down. Cache the volume/shortcut enumeration (10s TTL), computed without holding the lock, so it is not re-walked on every keystroke and a slow mount can't wedge concurrent listings on the mutex.

Tests: callWithTimeout (fast vs slow), handleListDir over a temp dir, and the volume cache TTL behavior.

title: feat(sequence_editor): timeline editor, native transitions, render progress, and audio
body:
## Summary

Brings the full **sequence_editor** improvement line onto `main`: a multi-track NLE-style timeline FrameSource that assembles clips into a finished video — cuts, transitions, layering, and audio crossfades — entirely inside a job graph, no external editor. Based directly on the current `main` tip; merges cleanly.

## What's included

- **Native Go transition engine** (`transition/`, ported from FFmpeg `vf_xfade.c`). Replaces push-fed libavfilter `xfade`, which corrupted the incoming clip's chroma (green cast). The full xfade set (wipes, slides, fades, circles, …) composites cleanly in pure Go; custom transitions are registerable. Adds `av.Frame` plane access + `NewVideoFrame`.

- **GUI timeline table editor.** The `sequence_editor` Inspector edits the output format and audio inline and opens a spreadsheet-style **Edit Timeline…** dialog (rows = clips), with buffered Apply/Cancel, live validation, a "Chain timeline" helper, and transition pickers fed by `GET /api/transitions` and `GET /api/audio-transitions`.

- **FrameSource render progress + ETA fix.** Source nodes that generate their own frames now record node metrics and emit `rendered X / N frames` progress. Fixed the aggregate progress/ETA so it tracks the rendered sequence's length, not an unconsumed source clip's duration.

- **Audio + auto-coupled crossfades.** `sequence_editor` mixes an audio stream from the same clips as the picture (opt-in via `format.sample_rate`), crossfading across each transition — auto-coupled to the clip's video transition, overridable per clip via `transition.audio` (`curve`/`duration`/`off`). Adds a native Go crossfade engine (`acrossfade/`, curves from `af_afade.c`), audio frame primitives in `av`, and the `processors.MultiStreamSource` interface so one FrameSource emits both a video and an audio stream routed to separate encoders.

- **Removed the redundant `xfade_sequence` processor.** It was a single-track montage built on the same abandoned push-fed-`xfade` mechanism (never got the native fix) and never shipped on `main`; `sequence_editor` is a strict superset. The O(1)-frame streaming-memory idea is noted as a future optimization at the reader cache.

- **Docs + examples.** New/rewritten: `docs/architecture/transitions.md` (engine + audio design), `docs/video-editing-guide.md` (single-tool, new-user walkthrough), `docs/using-mediamolder.md` §5.15, `docs/gui.md`, a first-class README capability section; runnable examples `61/62/63_sequence_editor_*.json`.

## Verification

- Go build, `go vet`, frontend `tsc`, and the affected test suites (`av`, `acrossfade`, `processors`, `job`, `internal/gui`) all pass.
- End-to-end verified on a real job: H.264 video + AAC audio, dual output streams, equal-power crossfade non-silent and dip-free.
- Embedded GUI bundle rebuilt.

## Notes

- A repo-wide pre-existing `gofmt` drift (~20 files in `av/`, `compat/`, `cmd/`, …) already present on `main` is intentionally **not** touched here — better addressed as a separate `style:` PR.

Remove testdata/BBB_10sec.mp4 and testdata/BBB_30sec.mp4 from Git LFS (176 MB combined) to reduce monthly LFS bandwidth consumption.

Add scripts/fetch-bbb.sh which downloads the full Big Buck Bunny 1080p stereo AVI (~733 MB) from Blender's CDN on demand. Tests seek directly into this file (ss=450, t=10 for 10-second tests) rather than relying on pre-trimmed clips.

CI caches the source file via actions/cache (key bbb-1080p-stereo-avi-v1) so it is fetched at most once per runner image. LFS pull is retained for the remaining small fixtures (sample.aac, sample.jpg, etc.).

The git checkout no longer triggers an LFS download for the two largest objects, cutting per-workflow LFS traffic from ~176 MB to ~0.

Signed-off-by: Tom Vaughan <tom@tvaughan.com>

title: av bindings for SEI NAL Unit + example sei adding processor
body:
Primary change — av package: frame side data API

The av package now exposes helpers to attach, read, and remove FFmpeg AVFrame side data, including typed paths for common cases:

Generic: AddSideData, SideData, AllSideData, RemoveSideData
User data unregistered SEI: AddSEIUnregisteredSideData, SEIUnregisteredSideData
Other helpers where relevant (e.g. A53 CC, S12M timecodes) and FrameSideDataType mirroring libavutil
Implementation lives in av/frame_sidedata.go, with tests in av/frame_sidedata_test.go.

Secondary — example processor

A small built-in processor sei_hello (processors/sei_hello.go + tests) demonstrates using AddSEIUnregisteredSideData on video frames (16-byte UUID + optional text, default "hello"). It is illustrative of the new av APIs, not the core library addition itself
